synopsis: NVIDIA is a significant platform dependency: most graphics cards named in the booklet are NVIDIA models because reviewed simulators rely on its ray-tracing libraries, while Chrono CRM terrain requires an NVIDIA GPU—a community-raised dependency risk, not a recommendation [f16192, f8500, f16193]. For sensor-ready assets, NVIDIA specifies separate non-visual material metadata because material behaviour can vary nonlinearly with wavelength and cannot be inferred from visual materials; its radar schema also models wavelength-dependent responses and indirect paths producing ghost detections [f3835, f3926, f3934, f3935]. Ansys/NVIDIA GTC 2020 vendor figures report 14 workstation CPU hours for a 12-second radar scenario and about 12 ms per frame for a GPU real-time version against a 30 fps target, but the supplied facts do not establish equivalent workloads [f4931, f4932]. Licensing descriptions require component-level care: Isaac Sim is described as Apache 2.0 with NVIDIA asset terms, while staff also described free use for teams of up to two; the relationship between those statements is not resolved here [f9014, f8485, f8903]. NVIDIA NuRec Gaussian splatting is integrated into Isaac Sim and CARLA 0.9.16 under an open-core model, while OpenUSD and Omniverse combine an open standard with NVIDIA components [f8609, f9162, f9167].
